In summary, our research is concerned with
how we can learn to use natural language to guide an agent to perform tasks in an unknown environment.
how to make the language acquisition process more efficient, and we show how this can be done by leveraging the agent’s own experience.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper proposes an approach for instruction following in reinforcement learning that uses language as a means of communication between the agent and the environment.
the proposed method is able to learn from its mistakes and improve its performance over time.
the proposed approach is a simple and effective way to improve instruction following agents in the BabyAI benchmark.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
THER can learn to follow instructions without the need of external demonstrations, and can learn to map states into language by observing past successes.
we are the first to propose an approach that can learn to follow language-based instructions without any expert demonstrations.

we propose an approach that combines language and reinforcement learning in a way that allows the agent to learn to follow instructions by itself, and we show that this approach can lead to improved performance compared to baselines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language is a natural fit to RL and that it can help to learn complex tasks without the need to rely on expert demonstrations or inductive biases.
the agent itself can learn how to generate instructions that match the trajectory, and that this approach can be used as an alternative to the current methods in language and RL.
